questions.prompt: What kind of tests make up Folio's server suite, and how does the FolioApiFactory harness work? Explain what most tests boot and exercise versus the few unit tests, how the in-memory SQLite database survives across per-request DbContexts, which environment and startup path the harness runs, how authenticated clients and database assertions are made, and how read-only and mutating tests are isolated.

keyPoints.text: Almost every server test boots the real API through FolioApiFactory and exercises HTTP endpoints end to end.
keyPoints.quote: boots the real API through `FolioApiFactory` and exercises HTTP endpoints end-to-end

keyPoints.text: A handful are pure unit or model tests that build a FolioDbContext directly, such as MigrationGuardTests.
keyPoints.quote: that build a `FolioDbContext` directly.

keyPoints.text: One in-memory SQLite connection stays open for the factory's lifetime, so schema and seed persist across scoped DbContexts.
keyPoints.quote: is opened and kept open for the factory's lifetime so the schema + seed persist across the scoped `DbContext` instances

keyPoints.text: The harness runs in Development, so Program's real startup path (migrate, then seed) runs against that connection.
keyPoints.quote: It runs in the **Development** environment, so `Program`'s startup path

keyPoints.text: CreateAuthenticatedClient logs in over the real login endpoint, so the whole auth path is exercised.
keyPoints.quote: so the whole auth path is exercised.

keyPoints.text: WithDbAsync runs an assertion against a fresh scoped FolioDbContext.
keyPoints.quote: runs an assertion against a fresh scoped `FolioDbContext`.

keyPoints.text: Read-only tests share one factory through IClassFixture.
keyPoints.quote: read-only tests share one factory via `IClassFixture<FolioApiFactory>`

keyPoints.text: Mutating tests create and dispose their own factory, so mutations never leak between cases.
keyPoints.quote: so mutations never leak between cases.

questions.prompt: How are Folio's client tests built? Explain what a component test renders and in what environment, what replaces the server, how installFetchMock resolves routes and what it returns, how a 204 is mocked, how a signed-in session is primed, which read-only UI states are covered for the Viewer role, and which command doubles as the typecheck gate.

keyPoints.text: Component tests render one component or small tree with React Testing Library in jsdom and assert on the accessible DOM.
keyPoints.quote: render a single component (or small tree) with React Testing Library in jsdom and assert on the accessible DOM.

keyPoints.text: No server runs: globalThis.fetch is stubbed.
keyPoints.quote: No server runs** — `globalThis.fetch` is stubbed.

keyPoints.text: installFetchMock maps "METHOD /path" or "/path" to a mocked Response and returns the vi.fn() so tests can assert requests.
keyPoints.quote: returns the `vi.fn()` so tests can assert requests.

keyPoints.text: 204 responses default to a null body, per the Fetch spec.
keyPoints.quote: responses default to a **null body** per the Fetch spec.

keyPoints.text: seedSession() primes a signed-in session in localStorage and the API client.
keyPoints.quote: primes a signed-in session in `localStorage` +

keyPoints.text: PermissionGating covers the read-only UI states for the Viewer role.
keyPoints.quote: (`PermissionGating`) UI states for the Viewer role.

keyPoints.text: pnpm build (tsc -b && vite build) is also the typecheck gate.
keyPoints.quote: tsc -b && vite build (also the typecheck gate)

questions.prompt: What trap do test harnesses built on EnsureCreated() fall into, and what do Folio's two MigrationGuardTests each check? How was the guard shown to catch real drift, and how does deliberately deleting the ExpectedVersion guard in PageService.UpdateAsync show that a single test pins that behavior? Finally, how can EF tooling build the context without running startup?

keyPoints.text: With EnsureCreated, a model change with no matching migration still works in tests while breaking a freshly migrated production database.
keyPoints.quote: still "works" in tests while breaking a freshly-migrated production database.

keyPoints.text: The model test diffs the live EF model against the migrations' model snapshot and fails on any pending change.
keyPoints.quote: diffs the live EF model against the migrations' model snapshot

keyPoints.text: The seeder test migrates a fresh database, seeds it, and pins that the seeder fits the migrated schema and is idempotent.
keyPoints.quote: pinning that the seeder is compatible with the migrated schema and that seeding is idempotent.

keyPoints.text: Adding an unmapped property made both guard tests fail: the diff test on the pending change, the seeder test on the missing column.
keyPoints.quote: both guard tests failed (the diff test on the pending change, the seeder test on the missing column)

keyPoints.text: Removing the ExpectedVersion guard makes exactly Page_update_with_stale_version_returns_409 fail.
keyPoints.quote: exactly `Page_update_with_stale_version_returns_409` fails

keyPoints.text: A design-time FolioDbContextFactory lets EF tooling build the context without running the API's migrate and seed startup.
keyPoints.quote: lets the EF tooling build the context without running the API's migrate/seed startup.
